PullRequest.Title: inline chat: add experimental Agent Host backend
PullRequest.Body:
inline chat: add experimental Agent Host backend

Adds an Agent Host backend for editor inline chat. The setting
`chat.inlineChat.agentHost.enabled` controls it and is off by default. When the setting is
off, inline chat operates as before.

The Agent Host writes files to disk. It does not stream edits into the editor. Inline chat
therefore builds its review UI from before/after snapshots.

- Adds `InlineChatSessionResolver`. It selects the Agent Host session or the legacy local
  session. It falls back to the legacy session on failure. It does not fall back when the
  user cancels.
- Extracts `IChatEditReviewSession` as a supertype of `IChatEditingSession`. A surface can
  supply reviewable entries without checkpoints, storage, streaming edits, or multi-diff.
  Editor review UI, such as decorations and keep/undo, continues to operate.
- Adds `InlineChatEditReviewSession`. It saves and snapshots the target file, makes the file
  read-only for the turn, and reuses `ChatEditingModifiedDocumentEntry`. Diff decorations and
  hunk review operate without new diff code.
- Shows diff decorations in real time. Each turn starts and stops external-edit mode, so disk
  reloads count as agent edits. The diff stays cumulative across turns.
- Tracks the files that the agent edits outside the target file. The Agent Host announces each
  edit when a tool call completes. The baseline content comes from that edit.
- Lets `IFilesConfigurationService.updateReadonly` accept an `IMarkdownString`. A programmatic
  lock can then show its own reason.
- Shows the current agent operation in the inline input placeholder.
- Keeps notebooks and untitled documents on the legacy path.

Makes throwaway (ephemeral) sessions start and run more quickly:

- Disables MCP servers, subagents, and custom agents for these sessions.
- Skips the turn-start checkpoint. This work is on the critical path of each turn.
- Skips title generation and the rename instruction. The title is never shown.
- Adds `enabledForEphemeralSessions` to server tool definitions. A tool must opt in before an
  ephemeral session receives it.

Also keeps throwaway sessions out of the session lists. The host no longer sends
`root/sessionAdded` for an ephemeral session. The chat history index no longer stores an
external session from a transient surface.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed event dependency, range-derived changing ID, watcher disposal/recreation, unique correlation IDs, and asynchronous provider boundary are all directly traced. Only the platform-specific duration of each watch registration is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem watcher registrations and provider watch operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One delete/add cycle and one uniquely correlated provider watch request per non-empty selection change; drag-selection and Shift+Arrow repeat this at input-event frequency, and asynchronous watcher setup can overlap.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive filesystem/IPC work and input latency while changing the inline-chat selection
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Inline chat did not mirror the editor selection into ChatAttachmentModel on each cursor-selection event, so changing the selection did not create or dispose file watchers.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new autorun rebuilds a file attachment whenever editorObs.cursorSelection changes and calls updateContext with the range-derived attachment ID.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 389 calls attachmentModel.updateContext for every cursorSelection invalidation; the immediately preceding asFileVariableEntry builds IDs as URI plus range, so each changed non-empty range deletes the old attachment and adds a new one.
Findings.Title: Reuse the file watcher while the selection range changes
Findings.Impact: With Agent Host inline chat open, adjusting a non-empty selection (dragging or Shift+Arrow) can issue a filesystem watch registration for every selection event, causing avoidable I/O/IPC churn and visible selection/input jank.
Findings.Evidence: ChatAttachmentModel.updateContext disposes the old attachment watcher and calls _watchAttachment for the added ID. _watchAttachment calls fileService.createWatcher; FileService assigns a fresh correlationId to every createWatcher call, includes it in the watch hash (preventing deduplication), and asynchronously invokes provider.watch. Thus rapid range changes fan out into overlapping provider watch registrations.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the attachment's file watcher stable while only its range changes, or coalesce/defer range updates until request submission; avoid deleting and re-adding the same URI attachment on every selection event.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Before sending every turn, ephemeral Agent Host sessions synchronously captured a turn-start checkpoint. For each working directory this opens session state, resolves the Git repository, captures the working tree through git status/read-tree/staging/write-tree subprocesses and temporary filesystem operations, and can initialize baseline commits.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Existing Agent Host terminal-chat ephemeral turns were blocked before provider send by repository-wide Git checkpoint work, with cost scaling by working-directory count and changed/untracked files.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added isEphemeralSession guard skips checkpoint capture entirely for transient sessions, removing the per-turn Git/database/filesystem work from the send critical path while durable sessions retain checkpoints.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: TerminalChatSessionResolver already creates Agent Host sessions with isEphemeral:true. AgentSideEffects awaited captureTurnStartCheckpoint immediately before agent.chats.sendMessage. AgentHostCheckpointService iterates all working directories and invokes captureWorkingTreeAsTree; that implementation runs git status, creates a temp index, stages changed paths, runs read-tree/write-tree, and deletes the temp directory. Added line 2235 guards this await for non-ephemeral sessions. Base blame resolves the old unconditional await to the supplied commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open editor inline chat with Agent Host disabled, or on notebook/untitled resources
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The controller now awaits createSession, but eligible resolution immediately starts a local ChatModel when the setting is off; notebook and non-file resources bypass the resolver. No filesystem, IPC, subprocess, database, or network operation was added to the session-creation critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One model/session per active inline-chat file; duplicate creation for the same URI is rejected after the await.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pending creation per controller, cancelled on rerun/close; a second split-editor creation is detected before insertion.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Local ChatModel creation is fresh per session; no cold remote session refresh or backend hydration is used.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: eligibility, setting gate, and fallback path are explicit in InlineChatSessionServiceImpl and InlineChatSessionResolver.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local model construction and extension activation costs are unchanged and not evidenced as material here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the default/off path preserves legacy local behavior apart from cancellable async orchestration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Agent Host-backed inline chat and send a focused edit turn
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening creates a provisional external session and acquires a ChatModel; backend materialization is deferred until the first request. Before each request reaches the provider, beginTurn may save a dirty target, acquires/creates the review model and read-only state, then Agent Host IPC/provider work runs. Completion reloads tracked editor models from disk before the per-session turn queue advances.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Save the target when dirty before allowing Agent Host edits
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero or one save per turn
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy inline chat streamed edits into the in-memory editing session and did not need this pre-turn disk save.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks provider send only when the target is dirty, preserving user data.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize/send the ephemeral session through Agent Host on first request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session materialization and one send per turn; no per-file fan-out
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor inline chat used the extension-host/local ChatModel path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required backend path when the experimental setting is enabled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider model request performed by the selected Agent Host backend
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider turn per submitted inline request
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The legacy inline agent invoked its provider through the extension-host path rather than Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dominates response latency but is intentional for the selected backend.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload each tracked model from disk at turn completion
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reload per accumulated tracked entry; normally one target file
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy inline chat already owned in-memory edits and did not reload Agent Host disk writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes review-state synchronization before the next queued turn begins.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Normally one target file and one request at a time; work grows with turns, dirty saves, and unique externally edited files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: InlineChatSessionService serializes turns with turnQueue. Agent Host turn handling is one provider send per request. Entry creation is coalesced per URI, while end-of-turn reloads are sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first turn creates the target entry and baseline; later turns reuse the entry and cumulative initial content. New external paths are cached in ResourceMaps, and concurrent creation for the same URI shares one in-flight promise.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: save, model creation, serialized queue, provider send, and reload calls are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual provider latency and file reload duration vary; focused instructions make the effective file cardinality one in the normal workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the disk synchronization boundaries are required by the new backend and are cached/serialized at normal one-file cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host announces edits outside the inline target
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each newly announced URI reads its before-content snapshot, creates one review model/entry, and all accumulated entries reload from disk at turn end.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read before-content snapshot and create a model reference for a newly edited external file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once concurrently per unique external URI, then cached
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The legacy inline path did not consume Agent Host external-edit announcements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed to make an off-target edit reviewable; processing occurs during the active turn and is awaited at turn end.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload accumulated external entries from disk
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per tracked URI per turn
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Agent Host disk-written external entries existed on editor inline chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serial before the next queued turn; normal cardinality remains one because inline instructions prohibit off-target edits.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unique external file URIs announced by tool completion after URI deduplication; repeated announcements reuse entries and in-flight creation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Response callbacks can overlap, but _externalEditEntriesInFlight coalesces entry creation per URI; processing within a scan and end-turn reloads are sequential, and turns are globally serialized for the session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Initial contents and entries are positively cached for the inline-session lifetime; misses read once per unique URI. There is no negative cache for failed reads, but only explicit external-edit announcements retry them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the scaling and boundaries; lower prevalence for broad off-target edits.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A misbehaving agent could edit many files, but the added host instruction explicitly restricts the operation to the target, so large fan-out is not the realistic expected workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: unique-path caching and in-flight coalescing bound creation work, and large external-file cardinality conflicts with the focused workflow.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change a non-empty editor selection while Agent Host inline chat is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every cursorSelection invalidation rebuilds the file attachment. Because the attachment ID includes the changing range, updateContext removes the old attachment and adds a new one, synchronously initiating a uniquely correlated asynchronous filesystem watch request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register and unregister a correlated non-recursive file watcher for the selected file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new provider watch registration per non-empty selection change
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inline chat did not mirror each selection change into ChatAttachmentModel, so cursor selection changes did not touch filesystem watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Triggered directly from the editor selection autorun and can contend with input/rendering while asynchronous registrations accumulate.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selection-change events, including every drag-selection update or Shift+Arrow keypress; one watcher dispose/create cycle per distinct range.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: There is no debounce or shared limiter. FileService starts doWatch asynchronously, so rapid events can leave multiple provider.watch setups in flight even though old watcher handles were disposed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: FileService normally hashes watch requests, but createWatcher assigns a fresh correlationId and includes it in the hash, so these same-URI requests cannot reuse the active watcher cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the range-derived ID, update/delete-add behavior, watcher creation, unique correlation key, and async provider call are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider watch registration cost varies by platform and remote filesystem, affecting severity but not the fan-out mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out; submitted as a finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run existing ephemeral Agent Host terminal-chat turns
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The PR now skips turn-start checkpoint capture before provider send, along with title/tool setup work for ephemeral sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Git repository discovery, status, read-tree, staging, write-tree, and possible baseline commit/ref operations
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously several Git subprocesses per working directory per ephemeral turn; now zero
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base revision unconditionally awaited checkpoint capture for terminal ephemeral sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously blocked agent.chats.sendMessage; removed from ephemeral turn critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/delete a temporary Git index and persist turn metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one temp-index lifecycle per Git working directory per turn; now zero for ephemeral sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Performed on each terminal ephemeral turn before provider send.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One checkpoint previously ran per turn and iterated every configured working directory, with Git cost scaling with changed/untracked paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Checkpoint capture is serialized per session and was synchronously awaited before send; the guard removes it rather than parallelizing it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository-root helpers may cache some discovery, but working-tree capture itself runs each turn. Ephemeral sessions now bypass it entirely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high; the existing terminal resolver marks sessions ephemeral and the old await is directly traced to Git/database operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact savings depend on repository size and working-directory count, but the subprocess/filesystem critical path is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: This PR fixes a real performance regression; the introducing commit was recorded through report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispose inline/terminal external chat sessions and update editor review discovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Transient external models are no longer written into chat history on disposal/shutdown. Review sessions are registered in-memory for decorations/actions, while full editing-session lookup uses a ResourceMap.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one storage update for a disposed transient external model with requests/draft; now zero for inline/terminal locations
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All non-local external sessions could enter the history persistence path regardless of surface.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removed from disposal/shutdown work for transient sessions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live transient sessions, editing sessions, open editors, and review entries. Eager editor controllers rescan review-session lists only when session/entry observables change, not for every streamed model edit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Persistence filtering is synchronous before storage writes. Registry notifications fan out through observables; no subprocess/IPC/network boundary is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Full editing sessions are keyed by resource for O(1) lookup; review sessions remain in the recency list and are removed with owner registration disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for persistence removal and registry behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical counts of simultaneously live inline review sessions are small; shutdown storage savings depend on usage.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: storage work is reduced, and the remaining in-memory scans have low realistic cardinality and no expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 57 changed files and relevant transitive paths. Submitted one medium boundary-fanout finding for per-selection filesystem watcher recreation. Recorded one verified regression fix for removing Git checkpoint work from ephemeral turns. Other new disk/model work is bounded by the focused one-file workflow, cached per URI, and serialized with explicit cleanup.
